title: a text hit on a whiteboard file renders twice, once by path and once by node moniker
body: `intent search "expired snapshot" --limit 8` renders each hit on a whiteboard file twice: once with the path in the second column and once with the node's moniker (`intent/whiteboard/cc/.history/20260815/inbox.vc.md:1987  file  intent/whiteboard/cc/.history/20260815/inbox.vc.md  ...` then the same line with `cc`; likewise `vc`, `ic`). Eight rows shown carry four distinct hits. Either the two rows are two records for one line (a file hit and a board hit) and one of them should not be a `file`, or the renderer prints one record twice. The `.history` archives dominating a text search's top rows is a separate question about the prose corpus, not filed here.
